newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: KL overnight rate at 6.5/7.0 pct, trading cautious.
newsitem.headline: KL overnight rate at 6.5/7.0 pct, trading cautious.

text.p: The overnight interbank rate was at 6.5/7.0 percent at 0800 GMT on Thursday in cautious trading as players focused on developments in Thailand, dealers said.

"The market is a bit uncertain at the moment as players are concerned about developments in Thailand. Until the dust settles, I think the market here will remain uncertain," said a dealer at a Malaysian bank.

The Thai baht fell sharply on Thursday after the resignation of Finance Minister Amnuay Viravan. News that Commerce Minister Narongchai Akrasanee also planned to tender his resignation could pull down the baht further, dealers said.
The overnight traded between 6.0 and 7.8 percent on Wednesday.
Dealers said some large local commercial banks were starting to get long, and this has also led to a drop in the overnight from its recent range.
"The banks were short earlier but they are getting long now," said one dealer.
He said lending by the central bank as well as maturity of Bank Negara bills worth one billion ringgit on Wednesday have helped ease market tightness. "Rates should start easing a bit," he said.
Another maturity of Bank Negara bills worth 500 million ringgit on Friday should further help improve market liquidity, though not for long.
Some dealers said there will be an outflow of around two billion ringgit on June 26 due to maturity of funds which Bank Negara lent to the market to help ease a liquidity squeeze last month.
Earlier, one-week money was at 7.80 percent against 7.70/80 percent on Wednesday.
One- and three-month money were steady at 7.8/8.0 percent.

Interest rate futures on the Malaysia Monetary Exchange were unchanged to higher on expectations of easing interest rates following news of a slower growth in money supply in April, futures market dealers said.
Bank Negara said on Wednesday broad money M3 grew by 19.7 percent in April against 21.0 percent in March.
At 0800 GMT, the three-month Kuala Lumpur Interbank Offered Rate (KLIBOR) December contract was unchanged at 92.64, or an implied yield of 7.36 percent.
The March 1998 contract rose one to 92.70, or 7.30 percent and June 1998 was up three to 92.72, or 7.28 percent.
